name: Methyldienolone (M-Dien)
lead: Methyldienolone (RU-3467) is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid, a 17-alpha-methylated 19-nortestosterone derivative.[1] It has not been marketed as a medicine. Published literature is sparse.
Wikipedia lists it as a US Schedule III substance and as prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency.[1]

paras: No studies found. Related laboratory work includes an environmental chemistry study of photolysis products of methyldienolone and dienogest, which found products with progestogenic and androgenic activity weaker than the parents,[2] and a 2026 study identifying metabolites with human liver microsomes for doping control.[3]

card.summary: An unmarketed oral 19-nor androgen; almost nothing published beyond detection chemistry.
card.note: Prohibited in sport; no human data found.

quick.overview:
Methyldienolone is an oral 19-nortestosterone derivative that was never marketed as a drug.

The literature consists of chemistry and doping-control papers.
quick.mechanism: It is classed as an androgen receptor agonist; no pharmacokinetic detail was found.
quick.risks: No adverse-effect data were found. It is prohibited in sport and listed as Schedule III in the US per Wikipedia.
